questions.q: What is the ITIL 4 purpose of the problem management practice?
options: To reduce the likelihood and impact of incidents by identifying actual and potential causes, and managing workarounds and known errors
To restore normal service operation as quickly as possible after a disruption
To authorize and schedule changes to the production environment
To log every incident reported by end users
questions.explain: Problem management targets root causes to prevent or reduce future incidents, unlike incident management's focus on fast restoration.

questions.q: What typically triggers problem identification, rather than a single isolated incident?
options: A pattern across multiple incidents, a major incident review, or a vendor-flagged known defect
Any time a user submits a service request
Only when a change fails during implementation
Problem identification happens automatically with no analysis required
questions.explain: A single incident rarely proves a problem exists; it's usually a trend, a major incident review, or an external signal that triggers investigation.

questions.q: What is a known error in ITIL 4 terms?
options: A problem that has been analyzed but not yet permanently resolved
An incident that has been resolved with a workaround
A change that failed during implementation
Any error message that appears in a system log
questions.explain: A known error is specifically a problem whose root cause is understood, with a permanent fix still pending.

questions.q: Which sub-practice is responsible for analyzing a problem's root cause and assigning it priority?
options: Problem control
Error control
Problem identification
Incident management
questions.explain: Problem control covers analysis and prioritization; error control manages known errors through to resolution afterward.

questions.q: A recurring incident keeps getting resolved quickly with the same workaround every time. What does this indicate about problem management's work on it?
options: The underlying root cause has not yet been permanently fixed, even though incident management keeps restoring service
Problem management has fully succeeded, since the workaround keeps users working
This means incident management is failing at its job
No problem record is needed as long as a workaround exists
questions.explain: Problem management is judged by whether the failure stops recurring, not by how fast any single occurrence is worked around.
